planDocument: dispatch://INFRA-522/artifact/plan-md (version 1): the full plan, with file:line readings, tasks T1-T6, the measure.py script and the acceptance table
summary: Split release-envoy-listener.yaml's docker job into a matrix of two native legs, `docker (amd64)` on ubuntu-24.04 and `docker (arm64)` on ubuntu-24.04-arm. Each leg builds, smoke-tests and pushes its own platform by digest (outputs push-by-digest, provenance mode=min, gha cache scope envoy-<arch>) and uploads its digest as artifact envoy-image-digest-<arch>. QEMU is removed. A new job `image_index` (packages: write only, no dependency code) validates the digests, joins them with `docker buildx imagetools create --metadata-file` into envoy:<sha>, outputs the index digest from the metadata file, and logs `imagetools inspect`. attest and release_publish take the digest from image_index. check-image-trigger-paths.sh allowlists the `outputs` input. Docs: workflow comments, packages/envoy/AGENTS.md, docs/solutions/envoy/ghcr-docker-multiarch-ci.md.

tasks.work: docker becomes `name: docker (${{ matrix.arch }})`, fail-fast, include {amd64: ubuntu-24.04, arm64: ubuntu-24.04-arm}, runs-on matrix.runner. Remove setup-qemu and the job outputs. setup-go `cache: ${{ matrix.arch == 'amd64' }}`. The smoke build gets cache-from type=gha,scope=envoy-<arch>. The publish step: platforms linux/<arch>, outputs type=image,name=ghcr.io/sjawhar/legion/envoy,push-by-digest=true,name-canonical=true,push=true, no push/tags inputs, cache-from/to with scope envoy-<arch> (mode=max). Add a digest-file step plus upload-artifact envoy-image-digest-<arch> (retention 1, if-no-files-found error; the comment says why the prefix is not legion-envoy-); the tripwire stays last. New job image_index: needs docker, ubuntu-24.04, permissions packages: write, outputs digest; download-artifact pattern envoy-image-digest-* merge-multiple; docker/login-action; one run step that validates the names (^[0-9a-f]{64}$), runs imagetools create --metadata-file --tag envoy:${{ github.sha }} with the two @sha256 sources, reads ."containerimage.descriptor".digest, checks ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$, writes the GITHUB_OUTPUT digest and runs imagetools inspect <image>@<digest>; values come through env. attest needs image_index. release_publish needs [build, image_index, release_build], its if tests needs.image_index.result == 'success', and OWN_DIGEST comes from image_index. Correct the comments at lines 47-58, 176-185, 217-229, 247-262, 403, 416 and 561-562.
Add "outputs" to BUILD_ACTION_INPUTS (line 519) with the comment: an exporter writes the result and names no input. Add an outputs: line to the with-known-inputs fixture (test.sh:708-718).

In AGENTS.md:3893-3936: native legs pushed by digest, joined by image_index; 'the digest `docker` handed over' becomes image_index; per-leg BuildKit provenance carried in the index. In the solution doc: rewrite §3 (QEMU) as the native-runner learning, and correct §1's 'workflow level' permissions sentence. No CHANGELOG entry and no .dispatch/architecture change (no workflow file added, renamed or deleted).

Locally, with UV_CACHE_DIR=$TMPDIR/uv-cache, run `uv run --no-project --with pyyaml==6.0.2 bash .github/scripts/<s>.sh` for check-image-trigger-paths, check-release-credentials, check-action-pins and check-private-names, and the .test.sh of the first two; all must pass. Negative control: without `outputs` in BUILD_ACTION_INPUTS, the check refuses with 'an input this check has not read'.

Commit subjects ci:/docs:. PR title `ci(envoy): build the arm64 Envoy image on a native arm64 runner` (never fix/perf/refactor: packages/envoy/AGENTS.md is in the envoy version pathspec and release-bump.sh:76 would cut an empty patch release). Body carries `Dispatch: INFRA-522`. From the final code head, run `gh workflow run release-envoy-listener.yaml -R sjawhar/legion --ref legion/INFRA-522` twice (cold, then warm), watching each with `gh run watch <id> -R sjawhar/legion --exit-status`. On 403 (no actions: write), report to the architect with the output at once.

PR body: before = measure.py over the 7 days before the merge (planner: 40.17 min over 94 runs, 2026-10-19..2026-10-27; two-platform step 34.59; spec's 41/36 cited); after = each dispatch run's id (cold/warm), per-leg minutes, slower leg, image_index and critical path; billed minutes before/after; note the two untagged per-platform indexes each run leaves in GHCR.

metric: Per run on main: the slower of the two `docker (<arch>)` legs' completed_at - started_at, over runs whose two legs both succeeded; the median is under 8 minutes. The old single `docker` job counts as its own slower leg for the before window. image_index and the critical path (first leg start to image_index end) are reported beside it, without a gate. Script: plan.md section 'The metric' (measure.py <start> <end> [branch], gh api --paginate --slurp).

decisionsForArchitect: The metric definition (slower leg per run) and the new job names `docker (amd64)`, `docker (arm64)` and `image_index`, which INFRA-519 and INFRA-524 must use for this line of INFRA-490.
The production check reports pending until merge + 7 days for A2; strictly, pending means production does not carry the merge yet.
Both legs smoke-test their own platform (uniform legs, about 0.7 min; the spec does not ask for it; today's comment says amd64 only).
The arm64 leg's setup-go uses cache: false, so no new setup-go-Linux-arm64 entry of about 0.5-1 GB grows the Actions cache against INFRA-490's under-9 GB target.
risks: That imagetools create keeps the per-platform attestation manifests is Docker's documented behaviour, unverified here. A1b/A1c on the first dispatch decide it; if they are missing, the implementer reports to the architect before going further.
The arm64 leg's speed and the mode=max cache export time are unmeasured; the warm dispatch run decides whether the slower leg stays under 8 min.

imagetools create --metadata-file needs buildx >= 0.32 (ubuntu-24.04 lists 0.38). If the flag is missing, add docker/setup-buildx-action to image_index, which is not dependency code under either check.
The implement App's actions: write for workflow_dispatch is unverified: past branch dispatches were by sjawhar-agent[bot].

findings.finding: The 7-day median cannot be proven at the first production-check look, and INFRA-524 also checks the same INFRA-490 line.
findings.answer: A2 is proven in the production check: the first look checks the first main run (A1a-A1e with the main identity, both legs' minutes); looks before merge + 7 days are pending, naming the window end; the first look after day 7 computes the median; the 336 h bound look always comes. Using pending this way is listed as a decision for the architect, and so is telling INFRA-519/524 the metric.

findings.finding: 'Docker job median' is undefined once docker is a matrix plus image_index; the baseline script matched name == 'docker', did not paginate and had no end date.
findings.answer: Metric decided: per run, the slower leg, median < 8; image_index and the critical path are reported without a gate. measure.py matches 'docker' or 'docker (', paginates with gh api --paginate --slurp, bounds created=<start>..<end>, and needs both legs successful. Checked by the planner: 40.17 min over 94 runs for 2026-10-19..2026-10-27.

findings.finding: The 'after' minutes before the merge can only come from branch dispatches, which start cold.
findings.answer: T5 dispatches twice (cold, then warm); T6 states both with run ids, labelled, and the before figure with its window and command; the Production: line adds the 7-day main median.

findings.finding: That imagetools create keeps the BuildKit attestation manifests is unverified; 'attestation' has two readings (GitHub attestation and BuildKit provenance), both consumed.
findings.answer: A1b-A1e prove both on the dispatch run and on the first main run: 2 attestation manifests naming the platform manifests, vcs:revision on both, and gh attestation verify (branch identity, with the main identity as negative control). The risk is recorded with a stop-and-report rule. The PR notes the orphaned per-leg indexes.

findings.finding: image_index should take the digest it pushed, not read it back by the mutable tag, and validate its artifacts as untrusted input.
findings.answer: image_index uses imagetools create --metadata-file and reads containerimage.descriptor.digest, checked against ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$; each downloaded digest file name is checked against ^[0-9a-f]{64}$; only this run's artifacts are downloaded; values reach the script through env.

findings.finding: Digest artifact names must not match legion-envoy-*, which release_publish downloads into the release assets.
findings.answer: The artifacts are named envoy-image-digest-<arch>, with a comment saying why.

findings.finding: The release_publish rewiring is not enforced by check rule 6 (OWN_DIGEST is in a step env).
findings.answer: T1 spells out needs [build, image_index, release_build], the if testing needs.image_index.result, OWN_DIGEST, attest's subject-digest, the comment at line 416, and removal of the matrix job's outputs.

findings.finding: check-image-trigger-paths.sh refuses `outputs`; it needs the allowlist entry, the fixture and no `push` beside `outputs`.
findings.answer: T2 adds outputs to BUILD_ACTION_INPUTS and to the with-known-inputs fixture; T1 deletes the push and tags inputs; T4 has the negative control. Per-arch tags are rejected because they publish tags consumers can see.

findings.finding: A per-arch gha cache scope is required; worker-image and this workflow already share the default scope.
findings.answer: scope=envoy-<arch> on the publish build's cache-from/to and the smoke build's cache-from; worker-image is left unchanged.

findings.finding: An arm64 setup-go cache entry would grow the Actions cache against INFRA-490's under-9 GB target.
findings.answer: The arm64 leg's setup-go uses cache: ${{ matrix.arch == 'amd64' }}; the implementer reports the smoke step cost and keeps cache: false unless the 8-min target would be missed. Listed as a decision for the architect. Removing QEMU also drops the 30 MB binfmt entry.

findings.finding: Smoke-testing arm64 is a scope decision and changes documented behaviour.
findings.answer: Both legs smoke-test their own platform; the workflow comment (176-185) and AGENTS.md change accordingly; an arm64 defect it finds is fixed in this PR; listed as a decision for the architect.

findings.finding: The implement App's right to workflow_dispatch is unverified.
findings.answer: T5 names the command; on 403 the implementer reports to the architect at once with the output; it dispatches from the final head and again after any later workflow push.

findings.answer: T1 lists every comment line range; T3 covers AGENTS.md and the solution doc (§3, plus §1's workflow-level permissions sentence); no change to .dispatch/architecture/release-engineering.md (paths are directories; no file added, renamed or deleted) or docs/kubernetes.md.

findings.finding: The PR title and commit types must not cut an empty envoy release (packages/envoy/AGENTS.md is in the version pathspec; release-bump.sh:76).
findings.answer: T5: subjects ci:/docs:, title ci(envoy): …, never fix/perf/refactor.

findings.finding: Several claims have no checked source: arm runners free, the spec's 41/36, buildx 0.38 and --metadata-file >= 0.32, imagetools keeping attestations, which platform the deployment's vcs:revision reader reads, the App's actions: write, and INFRA-519's job keys.
findings.answer: buildx: the planner read docker/buildx docs (the --metadata-file flag appears from v0.32) and actions/runner-images Ubuntu2404-Readme (Docker-Buildx 0.38.0), with a fallback in the risks. Baseline re-measured (40.17/34.59). The A1b-A1d dispatch run decides attestations, both platforms' provenance is proven, and the App's dispatch right has a 403 path. INFRA-519's keys go to the architect as a decision. That the runners are free is the spec's claim and changes no work.
